name: sol_basics_vi_svi_6
description: Solidity storage-write removal bug from conditional assembly return/stop in v0.8.13-0.8.16
question: The source file in `source` is written for a Solidity compiler version between 0.8.13 and 0.8.16 (inclusive) and contains a function that performs a storage write followed by a conditionally executed inline assembly block using return(...) or stop() to terminate execution early, such that the compiler could incorrectly optimize away the prior storage write due to the known storage-write-removal-before-conditional-termination bug, excluding code compiled with versions outside 0.8.13-0.8.16 or assembly blocks that unconditionally terminate at the very end of the function with no intervening control flow.
criteria: A function writes to a state variable and later contains an if-block whose body is an assembly block calling return(0,0) to exit early, with the pragma set to 0.8.13-0.8.16
A function updates storage then, inside a conditional branch, uses inline assembly with stop() to halt execution, compiled under solidity 0.8.14 or 0.8.15
A loop writes to a mapping or array slot each iteration and conditionally breaks out via an assembly return(...) statement depending on a runtime condition, under an affected compiler version
